hint.text: Coastal erosion is when the coastline is worn away by high sea levels, through the power of the waves and tides.
hint.label: Coastal erosion

atoms.a: The effects of climate change have increased coastal erosion.
Coastal erosion only happens during hot weather.

instruction.text: Why is it important to protect our coastlines? Read the text and select the matching image.

atoms.a: Coastlines provide habitats for different species of fish and birds in the area.
Coastlines absorb energy from storms and reduce damage to local infrastructure.
Coastlines help stop waste from washing into the ocean.

instruction.text: Let’s look at a case study of coastal erosion. Select Jacksonville on the map to learn more.

feedback.finish: Jacksonville is located in the north-east of Florida, along the Atlantic Ocean. The area has experienced severe coastal erosion in recent years.

atoms.b: Tropical ((++storms parties)) and hurricanes have been causes of major coastal erosion in and around Jacksonville.
High winds and strong waves from these storms washed away ((++sand sugar)) from the beaches and damaged dunes in the area.
The effects of coastal ((++erosion explosion)) in Jacksonville has greatly affected local infrastructure and ecosystems, as well as public safety.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: To combat the effects of coastal erosion, Jacksonville has invested in beach nourishment in coastal areas. This involves transporting sand from elsewhere and adding it to the beaches.

The local government then planted sea oats, whose roots make existing dunes more stable, as well as building sand fences to help with new dune formation. Dunes act as a natural barrier against waves during storms because they help to absorb the energy from waves.
